content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to the Apple assistant, set to debut with iOS 27. I've noticed one standout difference from other AI assistants, and it's on the positive side.

The new Siri in iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, setting it apart from other AI chatbots

I've been using Siri AI on the iOS 27 beta for nearly two months now, and so far it's done everything I expected of it.

The new generation Siri is far more powerful than its predecessor, delivering on its original promise of being a truly capable assistant on Apple devices.

But to be fair: if you need the most top-tier, cutting-edge AI tools, rivals like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be a better fit for you.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it with those third-party tools, I found one key difference that makes me lean strongly toward liking Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at excessive length, mimic human personalities, or trick you into forming a personal relationship with it.

Siri is useful and smart, and it does whatever you ask. But the way it responds makes it clear that it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you it's an AI, so it may make mistakes. It won't pretend to go on a date with you either.

By contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all full of personality and opinions, showing more human-like tendencies—but to me, that approach feels insincere.

I suppose some users prefer that more 'personalised' approach. But I much prefer AI assistants that stay in their lane and don't pretend to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world, but AI chatbots are tools, not people. I'm glad Apple understands this and has built the new Siri accordingly.

How human-like do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
